name: Ord
slug: Ord is a dragonborn paladin connected to the Great Eldarin Tree who serves as Gatekeeper of Feldspar.
description: Ord is a dragonborn paladin who joined Gerk’s group and became connected to the Great Eldarin Tree. He serves as the Gatekeeper of Feldspar, a realm he chose for its association with magic, science, alchemy, and experimentation, receiving its keystone after learning that Gilbrick had already been claimed.

log.summary: Ord joined Gerk’s group and accepted the new connection to the Great Eldarin Tree. After learning that Gilbrick had already been claimed, he chose **Feldspar** for its blend of magic, science, alchemy, and experimentation, receiving the Feldspar keystone and becoming its Gatekeeper. The Raven Queen evaluated Ord and Walker as less impressive than some of the other party members, though she still acknowledged that they had demonstrated something unusual to her.

log.summary: Ord remained near the central magical situation while deliberately staying as far from the immediate event as practical. While invisible, he investigated ways to reveal the position of someone affected by the disappearance effect, first considering powders or dust before realizing he could use his dragon vessel and olive oil. Spraying the oil produced a faint, visible silhouette of Ord, demonstrating that physical substances can outline an otherwise invisible person. The oil left a silent but physically present trail on the deck as it splashed and dripped. Ord also attempted to communicate in Draconic while investigating whether anyone was present, though no response was established.

log.summary: Ord stays with the main party on the invisible, silent boat rather than joining Walker's Reach excursion, his paladin magic noted as another potential source of exhaustion relief. Covered in oil from his dragon vessel and lacking detect magic, he instead casts See Invisibility after adding more oil, revealing Gerk, Sylan, Dana, the crew, the spectral door, and fading portal residue aboard the boat. He investigates the portal lines and steadies Sylan and Gerk with a persuasion check of fifteen, communicating with Sylan through blind eye speech when normal speech fails. Unable to physically interact with the spectral door, he proposes zone of truth before casting dispel magic on the effect suppressing sight and hearing rather than on the ship itself, successfully restoring visibility and sound. He asks Gerk to create a replacement door as Doorman, but Gerk refuses and asks Ord to stand nearby instead of Sylan while tempers settle.
notes: Not present with Walker's group; paladin magic could otherwise help reduce exhaustion.

log.summary: Ord dispelled the party's invisibility and silence; Dana says the spectral door appeared because he tried to open a door or thought about one. He went with Sylan, Gerk, and Dana to Carlkin, calling him a useful resource they have no reason to distrust. Allies he can see, including Carlkin and even a mouse, add his proficiency bonus to initiative (stated as +6, and once as +7); enemies do not. His initiative was 21, and Sylan's 26 and Dana's 22 include that bonus. Hold Monster failed: spell save DC 18, the creature saved, and it is immune to paralyzed. He spent his last 5th-level slot to concentrate on Holy Weapon on the Watcher's Mantle, which buzzed because the foe is extraplanar. A 24 hit for 16, plus 15 against an off-plane target and 21 from a 4th-level smite, severed the tentacle grasping Gerk in a mostly radiant arc. With Dana's inspiration and another 4th-level smite, a dimmer blow removed most of the tentacle on Sylan but left it intact. He dealt over a hundred damage that turn and had already used his bonus action. A grapple tied his Athletics of 25 and lost the tie, then struck for 19 and 12 bludgeoning; he had no reaction left to stomp. Play confirmed him as an Oath of the Watchers paladin, previously Oath of Vengeance. Disease immunity, Cleansing Touch, and his holy sword do not cover this mental effect. Beside the wall of eyes he failed a Wisdom save of 17, including +5, and expected to succumb. Vigilant Rebuke damages the source when an ally succeeds, even far away; he used his reaction once for 14 radiant damage, popping eyes on the door's edge. Pulled through a gap as pupils tracked him, he babbled about sea breezes and "my strength." After Gerk broke the floor he was left shoulder-deep in a roughly four-to-five-foot hole, looking up at the doorway of eyes. On a Wisdom save of 23, blinks showed a dock's edge and a younger dragonborn, and a melancholy voice offered to show his past if he gave them his future.
notes: He cast the dispel magic that removed the party's invisibility and silence. Dana says the spectral door appeared because he tried to open a door or thought about one.
He goes with Sylan, Gerk, and Dana to Carlkin. He says Carlkin has been a useful resource and that the party has no reason to distrust him.

Allies he can see, including Carlkin, add his proficiency bonus to initiative. The bonus is stated as +6, and one report also treats it as +7. It covers other living creatures he can see, which he describes as even a mouse that would have to survive, and it does not apply to the enemy. His own initiative is 21, bonus already included. Sylan's 26 and Dana's 22 include this bonus.
Hold Monster against the tentacles fails. His spell save DC is 18, the creature saves, and it is immune to the paralyzed condition.

He spends his last 5th-level spell slot to cast Holy Weapon, concentrating, on the Watcher's Mantle, expecting no further fights that day. The mantle buzzes because the foe is extraplanar. An attack of 24 deals 16, plus 15 because the target is not from this plane, plus 21 from a 4th-level smite (5d8), severing the tentacle grasping Gerk in a mostly radiant arc. He then spends Dana's inspiration and another 4th-level smite on the tentacle attacking Sylan. That second blow is dimmer, removes most of the tentacle, and leaves it intact. He deals over a hundred damage that turn and has already used his bonus action.

A tentacle tries to grapple him beside Sylan. His Athletics of 25 ties, and the tie goes to him, so it cannot hold him. The follow-up strikes deal 19 and then 12 bludgeoning. He has no reaction left to stomp.

He is confirmed in play as an Oath of the Watchers paladin; he previously had an Oath of Vengeance. Disease immunity, Cleansing Touch, and his holy sword do not cover this mental effect. Adjacent to the wall of eyes, he fails a Wisdom save of 17, including a +5 bonus, and expects to succumb.

Vigilant Rebuke lets him damage the source when an ally succeeds on the save, even if that source is far from him. He asks to trigger it for both successes. It costs his reaction, so he uses it once and deals 14 radiant damage, popping eyes on the edge of the door.

He steps into a gap between the eyes and is pulled bodily through. Pupils track him. He babbles incoherently about sea breezes and "my strength." After Gerk breaks the floor, the arm already inside the mass holds him up somewhat, and he is left shoulder-deep in a roughly four-to-five-foot hole, head and shoulders above ground, looking up at the doorway of eyes.
On a Wisdom save of 23, each blink shows him the edge of a dock and a younger dragonborn. A reverberating melancholy voice says they will show him his past if he gives them his future.

log.summary: Sylan is briefly unsure Ord is even present, then says he looks peaked after the attack and may need to sit down. When Carlkin asks where the girl is, Gerk answers with Ord's name, and who is actually in the room stays muddled. Carlkin sets a cup for him and calls his presence technical, which fits him being there without being plainly visible. The jug Carlkin pours from resembles one Ord produces from time to time.

log.summary: Ord is with Gerk and Sylan at Carlkin’s, then at the pub. At breakfast in the great hall he is eating a hot bun. Gerk looks to him before accepting Sylan as trainer and asks whether he will come along. He goes south into the forest to watch the doorway practice.

log.summary: Ord tests the fused lantern-staff in the woods: the Volga lantern joined, at his suggestion, to the staff from Shades and Trades. Lost strength from the fight with Gerk’s uncle became a rune-marked sphere, with Dana involved, and remains hidden in Gerk; he will seek a monk after the lantern. The hooded lantern has an evocation aura. On November 3, campaign year 25, it opened the Ethereal Plane and blinded him until lesser restoration. This time he shuts his eyes, a tone and flash light it, and he stays sighted. The world is grayscale and ghostly, hidden shadows appear, and his pupil-less eyes glow blue. A spirit grabs the crook and wails in his head. Divine Sense marks the spirits undead. He questions an elderly half-elf, accused of burning them with the light, then a sickly elderly woman who cannot give her name or her son’s. He releases both, and she is vacuumed away. He and Sylan think they are from Old Navel. After the black beacon he has wireframe sight to about sixty feet until he wills it off. Dana calls him Lord Bronztail; he says they were practicing and did not know what would happen.
notes: He still has not worked out the lantern and staff Sylan gave him. The lantern was found in Volga and is now fused with the staff Sylan found at Shades and Trades. He wants to test it in the woods, away from people, and he suggested the fusion. Ponchi is his roommate.

He has not regained his lost strength. He does not think the loss came from his duel with Gerk. The clearer account is the fight with Gerk's uncle: the strength was taken, a floating Ord appeared, and it solidified into a runic bead or rune-marked sphere, with Dana involved as it solidified. An earlier memory garbled the place as 'the orc Tam' and the object as 'a little Ord.' Dana's restoration and greater restoration did not work, because the strength is hidden in Gerk. He agrees that finding a monk who understands that fight is a good idea, after the lantern. Sylan remembers that Ord liked boats in a past life and offered Langdale, including a house or a boat, as a place to live.
He currently fights with a shield. Sylan pictures him using the sword and lantern together. He inspected the turquoise animal figurines from the white dragon hoard and left them behind.

The lantern is hooded and finely made. Detect Magic showed an aura of evocation. It has two settings; one blinded the whole room. A command word triggered an effect, undoing it triggered another, and the effect was hard to remove. On November 3, campaign year 25, he saw into the Ethereal Plane and blinded himself until Sylan used lesser restoration. He does not remember the inscription and offers 'Brightest day in darkness' as an ignition phrase. He also speaks an oath that no evil shall escape his sight.

This time he closes his eyes. Activation registers as an audible tone plus a flash, and he does not go blind. While the lantern is lit, the world is grayscale, semi-opaque, and ghostly, and he can see shadows in the woods that were hidden before. His eyes lose their pupils, glow the same desaturated blue as the lantern, and trail a little smoke when he blinks.

He tells Sylan about the figures, extends the staff toward the nearest one, and holds on when it grabs the crook. He asks if it can hear him and who it is. A wail answers inside his head. His nearby ward grants about +5 to a save from within 30 feet; Gerk uses it and still fails. He asks Sylan to grab the staff so he can get control back. He also keeps a hand on the staff and grapples one spirit, holding him against the pull.

He tries to end the effect by speaking the incantation backwards. He recalls that the last attempt to turn it off caused something else to happen. That backward attempt is not carried through. Toasting these spirits during the earlier ethereal sight is what set up the current vacuum.

He identifies the grabbed spirit, aloud, as an elderly half-elf. Divine Sense, which he has used once before, in Volga, reads the spirits as undead with no subtype. Strong evil smells noxious. The spirit accuses the one who shed the light of burning them, which points at Ord's earlier use. He questions the spirit about who he is, where his abode is, and who stole from him, then lets him go when Sylan says to.

He grabs the last spirit, a sickly elderly woman, and tries to learn her name and her son's so he can pass a message. She cannot answer. He says they are not getting anywhere and lets her go. While he is interacting with her she can death-grip his hand; when he consciously releases her, she dematerializes and is vacuumed away. He and Sylan think the spirits are from Old Navel.

He and Sylan had their hands together on the staff when the black beacon went up. After he lets Sylan release it, Ord still has a wireframe-style sight: movement and silhouettes out to about sixty feet, and no further spirits approach. He ends that sight by intending it. A long blink restores normal vision.
Dana addresses him as Lord Bronztail and demands to know what he was doing. He says they were practicing and did not know what would happen.

log.summary: Ord repeats the lantern-staff incantation. It blinds others, shows him the Ethereal Plane in grayscale, and lets him see the spirits on Sylan. He reads an evocation aura, calls their gripes possible unfinished business, gives Sylan the fused lantern-staff to test another user, and agrees to pass on the unspoken activation word. He asks how Gerk can be bad cop without threats, then says Gerk is strong of body. He flies to Carlkin's lighthouse with Dana, Walker, and Ciri; Araden taps his chest, calls him young Lane, and says his wings are in there. In the Sunder Chase he dispelled magic on another ship. Carlkin calls it clever, unseen for generations, and disqualifying; Ord says someone else would have thought of it. Sylan tells Haldor that Ord worked the lantern in Trigash, and Gerk says Sylan's hoard staff blinded him as the spirits entered. Ord remembers the first spirit wanting to return to Sylan, a scared woman who wanted help and would not go back, and struck spirits becoming tangible and changing. He recognizes Ledzbika. He is among those Erwin saw fly toward Trigash and back, and does not commit to lesser restoration for a hung-over Carlkin.
notes: He repeats the lantern-staff incantation while looking at it. It blinds others, shows him the Ethereal Plane in grayscale, and lets him see the spirits attached to Sylan. He reads an evocation aura and calls their gripes possible unfinished business.
He gives Sylan the fused lantern-staff to test whether another user changes the effect, and agrees to pass on the activation word. The word is not spoken here.
He asks how Gerk can be bad cop if he cannot threaten anyone, then tells Gerk he is at least strong of body.
He flies to Carlkin's lighthouse with Dana, Walker, and Ciri. Araden taps his chest, calls him young Lane, and says his wings are in there.

In the Sunder Chase he dispelled magic on another ship. Carlkin calls that a clever use of the talent, unseen for several generations, and the sort of thing that would get a competitor disqualified. Ord says someone else would have thought of it eventually.
Sylan tells Haldor that Ord was working the lantern in Trigash. Gerk says Sylan was also using the hoard staff and blinded him as the spirits entered Sylan.

He remembers the first spirit disliking the party and wanting to be given back to Sylan, and a woman who was scared, wanted help, and did not want to go back. He recognizes Ledzbika. He remembers that struck spirits became partly tangible and started changing.
He is among the group Erwin saw fly toward Trigash and back. He does not commit when Sylan suggests lesser restoration for a hung-over Carlkin.
